llm.summary: This skill is a clearly disclosed self-hosted speech-service helper, with real privacy and deployment risks that are documented and purpose-aligned.

dimensions.detail: The skill can process sensitive speech/text and uses server-side URL fetching; this is expected for the product, but users should configure auth, TLS or local binding, and private-download blocking when exposed beyond trusted local networks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses documented docker run commands for CPU or CUDA images, with disclosed bind mounts, ports, model downloads, auth configuration, and update/management commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly warn that audio, text, cloned-voice samples, and staged files go to the configured TALKIES_URL and should only be used with trusted instances, authorized voice samples, and user-approved workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Staged uploads, cached URL downloads, custom voices, and model files persist under the Talkies data directory; the artifact clearly discloses that staged files are shared, enumerable, and must be cleaned up by the caller.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The network, shell, Docker, ASR/TTS, voice cloning, file staging, MCP, and model-management capabilities match the stated purpose of operating and using a self-hosted Talkies speech service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use a Talkies server you operate or explicitly trust. Set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for shared or non-local deployments, prefer HTTPS or loopback binding, enable private-download blocking if untrusted users can submit URLs, avoid sending confidential text/audio to untrusted endpoints, and only use voice cloning with explicit speaker consent. Clean up staged files because they persist and are shared on the server.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The TTS examples send input text to the configured Talkies endpoint, which is expected for a remote or self-hosted speech API and is prominently disclosed as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The voice-cloning example uses reference voice material and synthesized text through the Talkies service; the artifact repeatedly documents consent requirements and warns against unauthorized impersonation.
[E1] expected: Additional speech examples repeat the same external transmission pattern; this remains a privacy consideration, but it is not hidden or purpose-mismatched in the inspected artifact.
